A kingdom is not necessarily close in size to all the earth. This minimizes the reach David describes.
Saying David used two pictures because one was not enough invents his reason for choosing them.
The explanation is a flat restatement, with little of Papa Dorin's personality in a moment that could be lively.
The allusion to Papa Dorin knowing darkness leaves his drawer backstory unstated, so a baker unfamiliar with it may miss the connection.

The psalm says there is great reward in keeping the LORD's words; it does not say David has received that reward.
Saying the LORD's words give David a reward omits the psalm's condition: the great reward is in keeping them.
David's question does not state that nobody can discern any of their own errors. The explanation makes an absolute claim the text does not.
